title: Nematic order in monomer-dimer models of Heilmann and Lieb with lateral attraction in dimensions $d\ge 2$
abstract: We study the $d$-dimensional generalization of Models II ($d=2$) and V ($d=3$) for liquid crystals introduced by Heilmann--Lieb (1979), which consists of dimers on the hypercubic lattice at chemical potential $μ$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction between parallel dimers with coupling constant $b>0$. For $d\in\{2,3\}$, these models were conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperatures provided that $μ+2(d-1)b>0$. We establish nematic order for all $d\ge 2$ under the additional condition $(4d-6)b>μ$, which corresponds to the physical regime in which misaligned dimers are rare on scales comparable to the correlation length of the one-dimensional reference system. While the treatment of orientational order here follows the approach of our recent work on Model I, the proof of the absence of translational order relies on a custom implementation of cluster swapping in the sense of Sheffield (2005). Consequently, we deduce uniqueness of Gibbs measure and anisotropic exponential decay of correlations within each oriented phase.
summary: This paper proves the existence of nematic liquid-crystalline order in generalized monomer-dimer models on the $d$-dimensional lattice. It achieves this by establishing the uniqueness of the Gibbs measure and proving the exponential decay of correlations using advanced techniques like cluster swapping. The results provide a rigorous mathematical characterization of orientational order in these lattice models.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously establish the existence and properties of nematic order in $d$-dimensional monomer-dimer models of liquid crystals.
main_result: Under specific conditions on the chemical potential ($\mu$) and attraction strength ($b$), the model admits a unique Gibbs measure exhibiting anisotropic exponential decay of correlations within the oriented phase.
method: The proof combines techniques from statistical mechanics, including cluster swapping, strong-percolation frameworks, and bounding probabilities of local configurations using mesoscopic box estimates.
model_or_system: The system is a monomer-dimer model on the $d$-dimensional hypercubic lattice ($\mathbb{Z}^d$), describing liquid crystals. The Hamiltonian includes terms for the number of dimers ($\mu$) and a lateral attraction ($b$) between parallel dimers.
key_observables: The primary observables are the probabilities of observing aligned versus misaligned dimers in the ordered phase, and the decay rate of correlations.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the chemical potential $\mu$, the coupling constant $b$, and the dimension $d$. The analysis requires the conditions $(4d-6)b > \mu$ and $\mu + 2(d-1)b > 0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a critical inverse temperature $ eta_d$ and the assumption that the relevant clusters are rare enough to be controlled by the cluster swapping technique.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a typical configuration of Model V on a torus, providing visual evidence of the predicted nematic order.
paper_structure: The paper generalizes Heilmann-Lieb's models to $d \ge 2$. It first establishes the mathematical framework using strong-percolation and then uses cluster swapping to prove the uniqueness of the Gibbs measure and the exponential decay of correlations in the ordered phase.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical techniques used (e.g., bounding correlations, proving uniqueness of Gibbs measures) are foundational to understanding phase transitions in complex many-body quantum systems.
